svg.title: The mask follows the load through the core
svg.desc: A detailed native RISC-V O3 datapath follows the same record and property loads. Fetch, decode, rename and dispatch feed an issue queue. I1 waits for I0's renamed P17 operand. Both use the AGU, LSQ, address translation and private caches; returned bytes are assembled or written back to the appropriate register. Per-instruction hints stay in the ROB. Private misses expose only observations at the LLC, while a separate bounded retirement channel can update resident metadata even for private hits. No host-side future lookup supplies the operand.
svg.text: The mask follows the load through the core
Blue carries addresses and values; purple carries dependencies and reuse state; green controls execution.
Same access: u=8 | CSR j=18 | request s=19 | property v=18 | line B
Native I0 reads 0x10000012; I1 returns p[18] = 1/128. P_B denotes its translated physical line.
RISC-V O3 core: two dependent loads
PROPERTY: s19, D26, ctx1, own PA
Receiver position advances only when a timed update arrives.
A private hit can bypass LLC data traffic, but still exports its own committed prediction. Squashed loads export none.
Observations never install FINITE/DEAD. Metadata updates never allocate or alter a data line.
The native model uses a dedicated metadata link and tag port; prefetch and physical-cost qualification remain separate.
